source: Backup and Recovery Procedures - SSA Infrastructure

chunks.title: SSA Backup Environment — Servers in Scope
chunks.content:
The SSA backup environment covers four servers:

A) Windows Server 2019 — "win-cube": Hosts SQL Server Express instance (localhost\SQLEXPRESS), IIS websites content (C:\Websites), and file shares source (C:\Shares with subfolders: Company, Finance, Temp, Users). Automation via Scheduled Tasks executing PowerShell scripts for SQL + IIS + file syncs.

B) Windows Server 2012 R2 — "DpathServer": Protected via IONOS Backup Unit Manager plan "Daily DC Protection (30 Days)". Separate from win-cube scripted Wasabi copies.

C) Ubuntu — "ubuntu": Protected via IONOS Backup Unit Manager plan "Daily DC Protection (30 Days)". Additional scripted backups write to Wasabi under wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/...

D) Windows Server 2022 — "SERVER_22": Uses Windows Server Backup (WSB) for nightly local backups to dedicated target volume F: (label WSB_BACKUP). Schedule: 20:00 daily. Scope: allCritical + systemState.

chunks.title: Wasabi S3 Buckets and rclone Remotes — Overview
chunks.content:
Two Wasabi S3 buckets are in use:

1) wasabi-backup-ssa — General backup bucket (non-versioned). Used for SQL backups (tiered), IIS website ZIP backups, and Linux tar/sql.gz style backups under linux/.

2) ssa-backup-prod — Versioning bucket used for "live files" backups. Wasabi bucket versioning provides historical recovery instead of script-managed versions.

Known rclone remotes (configured in C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf on Windows):

- wasabi-u: — General S3 remote for non-versioned bucket access. Endpoint: s3.wasabisys.com. Used for SQL, websites, and linux artifacts.
- wasabi-lock: — Versioned bucket remote. Endpoint: s3.us-central-1.wasabisys.com. Used for live file backups with Wasabi versioning.
- wasabi-linux: — Ubuntu S3 remote (endpoint s3.wasabisys.com) used by /opt/backup/server_backup.sh.

Security: Never store access keys, secret keys, passwords, or MFA codes in knowledge files. Store secrets only in protected locations and reference file paths only.

chunks.title: Win-Cube SQL Server Backups — Active Job Details
chunks.content:
Task name: SQLServer → Wasabi Backups (Tiered)
Runs as: SYSTEM (ServiceAccount), RunLevel Highest
Action: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\Backups\Backup-SqlServer-To-Wasabi.ps1"
Schedule: daily at ~6:00 PM

Active remote root: wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/databases

Active layout: wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/databases/{daily|weekly|monthly}/{DatabaseName}/{DatabaseName}_Backup_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.bak

Example: wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/databases/weekly/SuperiorState/SuperiorState_Backup_20251214_1101.bak

Local staging: C:\Backups\Databases\{Database}_Backup_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.bak
Log folder: C:\Backups\Logs\Wasabi-SQL-Backup_*.log
Rolling log: C:\Backups\Logs\Wasabi-SQL-Backup.log

Behavior: Script tries WITH COMPRESSION first. SQL Express does not support backup compression — it fails and the script retries WITHOUT compression. This is expected.

chunks.title: SQL Backup Fails Under SYSTEM — Root Cause and Fix
chunks.content:
Symptom: When the SQL backup scheduled task runs as SYSTEM, the run log shows errors like:
- Msg 916 ... NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM is not able to access the database ... under the current security context.
- Msg 262 ... BACKUP DATABASE permission denied in database ...
- Backup file not found after BACKUP (because BACKUP failed)

Root cause: The task runs as SYSTEM, but SQL Server doesn't treat NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM as sysadmin by default.

Fix (proven — run once as a sysadmin with -E):

IF IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin', 'NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM') = 0
BEGIN
  ALTER SERVER ROLE [sysadmin] ADD MEMBER [NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM];
END;

Optional: ensure the computer account exists as a login:
IF SUSER_ID('SUPERIORSTATE\WIN-BAFAS9DBTQ8$') IS NULL
BEGIN
  CREATE LOGIN [SUPERIORSTATE\WIN-BAFAS9DBTQ8$] FROM WINDOWS;
END;
IF IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin', 'SUPERIORSTATE\WIN-BAFAS9DBTQ8$') = 0
BEGIN
  ALTER SERVER ROLE [sysadmin] ADD MEMBER [SUPERIORSTATE\WIN-BAFAS9DBTQ8$];
END;

Validation: Run the task manually and check LastTaskResult is 0:
Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SQLServer → Wasabi Backups (Tiered)"
Start-Sleep 60
Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName "SQLServer → Wasabi Backups (Tiered)" | Format-List LastRunTime,LastTaskResult

chunks.title: SQL Express WITH COMPRESSION Fallback Behavior
chunks.content:
Symptom: SQL backup log shows: Msg 1844 ... BACKUP DATABASE WITH COMPRESSION is not supported on Express Edition

This is expected behavior. SQL Express does not support backup compression.

The backup script is designed to:
1) Try WITH COMPRESSION first
2) If the .bak file is not produced, retry WITHOUT COMPRESSION

Validation: In the run log, look for:
- "Primary backup didn't produce a file; retrying WITHOUT COMPRESSION (likely Express edition)."
- followed by "BACKUP DATABASE successfully processed ..."

As long as the retry succeeds and produces a .bak file, the Msg 1844 error is benign and can be ignored.

chunks.title: Testing SYSTEM Account Access — Method and Patterns
chunks.content:
When changing tasks to run as SYSTEM, you must confirm SYSTEM can:
- Decrypt SMTP secret (AES-keyed SecureString)
- Query SQL via integrated auth (sqlcmd -E)
- Write to C:\Backups\Databases
- Access rclone config + Wasabi remote

Method (proven, no PsExec needed):
1) Write a small test script to C:\Temp\*.ps1
2) Create a one-time scheduled task running as SYSTEM
3) Redirect output to C:\Temp\*.txt
4) Schedule 1 minute ahead to avoid "earlier than current time" warning

Example pattern:
$st = (Get-Date).AddMinutes(1).ToString('HH:mm')
schtasks /create /f /tn "\Temp\TEST" /sc once /st $st /ru "SYSTEM" /tr "cmd.exe /c powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Temp\test.ps1 > C:\Temp\test.txt 2>&1"
schtasks /run /tn "\Temp\TEST"
Start-Sleep 5
Get-Content C:\Temp\test.txt

Cleanup after tests:
schtasks /delete /f /tn "\Temp\SYSTEM_SQL_TEST"
Remove-Item -Force C:\Temp\system_*_test.ps1,C:\Temp\system_*_test.txt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

All four checks (SMTP, SQL, disk write, rclone) were validated successfully using this pattern on win-cube.

chunks.title: Scheduled Task Invocation and Quoting Issues
chunks.content:
Symptom: schtasks /create ... /tr "..." fails with ERROR: Invalid argument/option when task names contain special characters (like arrow glyphs →).

Fix pattern (reliable):
1) Put the logic in a .ps1 file
2) Use cmd.exe /c powershell.exe -File <script> > <output> 2>&1

For querying tasks with special characters in names, always prefer PowerShell cmdlets:
- Get-ScheduledTask (instead of schtasks /query)
- Get-ScheduledTaskInfo (for last run info)
- Start-ScheduledTask (to trigger manually)

These PowerShell cmdlets handle Unicode/special characters correctly where schtasks.exe may fail.

chunks.title: rclone Hangs on Large Directory Listings
chunks.content:
Symptom: Commands like lsl --recursive or deep lsjson --recursive over a very large prefix (tens of thousands of objects) can appear stuck or take a very long time.

Safer approaches:

1) Validate a single known object:
rclone lsl "wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/windows/win-cube/files/live/Company/er sigs/1stpiedmont.PNG" --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

2) Measure subtree size (fast sanity check):
rclone size "wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/windows/win-cube/files/live/Company/er sigs" --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf --fast-list

3) Limit depth:
rclone lsl "wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/files/live" --max-depth 2 --config ...

4) Compare file lists between prefixes (only when subtree is reasonable):
$old = rclone lsf "wasabi-u:..." --files-only --recursive --config $cfg
$new = rclone lsf "wasabi-lock:..." --files-only --recursive --config $cfg
Compare-Object ($old|sort) ($new|sort)

Key flags: --fast-list for S3 listings, --max-depth N when sampling, avoid unbounded recursive listings on 50k+ object trees.

chunks.title: S3 Case Sensitivity and Path Hygiene
chunks.content:
S3 object keys are case-sensitive. Windows paths are case-insensitive.

In this environment, both of these exist and represent SEPARATE keys:
- .../company/er sigs/... (legacy, lowercase)
- .../Company/er sigs/... (active, title case)

Observations:
- Legacy wasabi-backup-ssa used lowercase: company/...
- Active ssa-backup-prod uses title case: Company/...

Best practice:
- Treat the destination casing as canonical
- Do not "rename by case" unless intentionally migrating
- When comparing legacy vs active, always compare exact casing
- Standardize on a single canonical casing convention for live trees (current active uses Title Case in ssa-backup-prod)

chunks.title: Ubuntu Backup Discovery — Baseline and Identity
chunks.content:
When discovering Ubuntu backup configuration, start with baseline commands:

hostname -f
uname -a
lsb_release -a 2>/dev/null || cat /etc/os-release
date
whoami
id

Record: Hostname/FQDN, Distro + version, Timezone / clock sanity.

This establishes the identity of the server before diving into backup-specific discovery steps.

chunks.title: Ubuntu — IONOS Acronis Agent Discovery
chunks.content:
To check if the IONOS Backup Unit (Acronis) agent is installed and running on Ubuntu:

Service status:
systemctl status acronis* 2>/dev/null || true
systemctl status mms 2>/dev/null || true
systemctl status | grep -i acronis || true
ps aux | grep -iE 'acronis|mms' | grep -v grep || true

Installed packages:
dpkg -l | grep -i acronis || true
rpm -qa | grep -i acronis || true

Agent logs:
sudo find /var/log -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -iname '*acronis*' -o -iname '*mms*' \) 2>/dev/null
sudo journalctl -u mms --no-pager -n 200 2>/dev/null || true

Goal: Confirm the agent is installed, identify service name(s), and identify log location(s).

chunks.content:
Locate rclone binary:

Locate config (common paths):
- ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf
- /root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf

chunks.title: Ubuntu — Recommended Naming and Retention Targets
chunks.content:
Recommended naming patterns (align with what already exists):
- DB dump: beta_ssa_YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM.sql.gz
- Webapps tar: webapps_YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM.tar.gz
- Configs tar: configs_YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM.tar.gz

Target retention scheme (example):
- Daily: keep 14–30
- Weekly: keep 8–12
- Monthly: keep 6–12

Implement after discovery confirms how jobs run today.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Troubleshooting — Common Symptoms and Causes
chunks.content:
Symptom → Likely cause:

- Remote objects stop updating: cron/timer not firing, credentials expired/endpoint changed, network/DNS outage, disk full (staging)
- Artifacts too small: empty dump (mysqldump failed but wrote header), tar excluded paths / permission issues
- Job hangs: massive file tree enumeration, slow disk / IO bottleneck, rclone --fast-list missing for deep trees

Minimal safe diagnostics:
sudo df -h
sudo free -h
sudo dmesg | tail -n 50
sudo journalctl -xe --no-pager | tail -n 80

Known Ubuntu-specific issues:
- Acronis/agent libs can break mysql client with GLIBCXX errors; use clean env or mysqldump-clean helper
- mysqldump may fail with ERROR 1356 (broken views); fix by dropping/correcting views using admin creds
- "Paste freezes" can be XON/XOFF; stty -ixon prevents this

chunks.title: SERVER_22 — Windows Server Backup (WSB) Configuration
chunks.content:
SERVER_22 uses Windows Server Backup (WSB) for local disk backups.

Schedule: daily at 20:00
Backup scope: All critical volumes (bare metal recovery / BMR) + System state
Target drive: F: (volume label: WSB_BACKUP, approx 460 GB)
VSS option: COPY

Configured with:
wbadmin enable backup -addtarget:F: -allCritical -systemState -schedule:20:00 -quiet

This is separate from the Wasabi/rclone backup workflows. It provides local disk-based recovery for SERVER_22.

chunks.title: SERVER_22 — WSB Verification Commands
chunks.content:
Read-only verification commands for SERVER_22 WSB:

Confirm nothing is currently running:
wbadmin get status
Expected when idle: "No backup or recovery operation is currently running."

Enumerate backups on target (if local catalog is present):
wbadmin get versions

Enumerate backups (explicit target, always works after catalog reset):
wbadmin get versions -backuptarget:F:
Expected: One or more "Version identifier" entries.

IMPORTANT: A catalog reset (wbadmin delete catalog -quiet) was performed. This deletes the local WSB catalog/index but does NOT delete backup data on F:. After a catalog reset, always use:
wbadmin get versions -backuptarget:F:
...to re-discover what exists on the target.

chunks.title: SERVER_22 — WSB Common Failure Modes
chunks.content:
A) WSB fails because the target is not available:
Symptoms: Errors indicating the backup target could not be found.
Checks:
- Confirm F: is mounted and labeled WSB_BACKUP (Disk/Volume management)
- Confirm sufficient free space on F:

B) "No backups found" after catalog reset:
Checks:
- Use wbadmin get versions -backuptarget:F: (explicit target, required after catalog reset)
- Confirm the WSB backup folder exists on F: (WSB typically writes under \WindowsImageBackup\...)

No legacy WSB targets have been identified yet for SERVER_22. If another backup disk/path exists historically, treat it as Unknown until verified with wbadmin get versions -backuptarget:<drive>.

chunks.title: IONOS Acronis — Vulnerability Assessment Failure 0x80240438
chunks.content:
Symptom: Acronis/IONOS console shows:
- "Scanning Windows for vulnerabilities" → failed
- Error: Windows Update Agent returned an error 0x80240438

Observed on: WIN-BAFAS9DBTQ8.superiorstate.local (win-cube)

What was confirmed:
- WSUS policy values were not set (WUServer blank, WUStatusServer blank, UseWUServer blank)
- Windows Update COM search returned within 120s and showed pending updates
- Registry: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate has no WUServer, WUStatusServer, UseWUServer

Interpretation: Windows Update works but the vulnerability scan feature may be sensitive to Windows Update configuration, servicing stack state, proxy, or enterprise policy. Treat as non-blocking — backups can still succeed.

Useful verification:
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate" /s

Update Agent responsiveness quick check (PowerShell):
$s = New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session
$u = $s.CreateUpdateSearcher()
$r = $u.Search("IsInstalled=0 and Type='Software'")
$r.Updates.Count

chunks.title: rclone Verification — Compare Legacy vs Active Paths
chunks.content:
To confirm a specific file exists in both legacy and active (for spot-checking only):

$cfg = "C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf"

# OLD legacy
C:\rclone\rclone.exe lsl "wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/files/live/company/er sigs/1stpiedmont.PNG" --config $cfg

C:\rclone\rclone.exe lsl "wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/windows/win-cube/files/live/Company/er sigs/1stpiedmont.PNG" --config $cfg

Interpreting results:
- If timestamps/sizes match, it's likely a duplicated historical copy
- If new bucket has more files (e.g., closeit.PNG exists only in new), it suggests new path is the real "living" one

Note the case difference: legacy uses lowercase (company/), active uses title case (Company/).

chunks.title: Known Healthy Backup Outcomes — What Success Looks Like
chunks.content:
SQL job log shows for each DB:
- Backup completes
- Upload completes
- Retention completes
- Email subject indicates OK

Websites backup shows:
- weekly has last 3 zips
- monthly has one per month (last ~4 + current)

Files backup (versioned bucket) shows:

- JSON log has expected "Copied (new)" or "Copied (replaced existing)" lines

SERVER_22 WSB:

IONOS Backup Unit Manager:

chunks.title: Script Hardening Best Practices
chunks.content:
Best practices for backup script reliability:

- Prefer running scheduled tasks as SYSTEM for unattended reliability
- For SQL job under SYSTEM: ensure SQL permissions for NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (sysadmin); keep compression-first + fallback for Express
- For rclone jobs: include log file paths in email; avoid deep listings unless scoped (use targeted object checks, size --fast-list, and bounded --max-depth)
- Avoid complicated inline quoting in schtasks; put logic in .ps1 files instead
- Use PowerShell cmdlets (Get-ScheduledTask) instead of schtasks.exe for task names with special characters
- For Ubuntu: use mysqldump-clean wrapper to avoid GLIBCXX conflicts from Acronis agent libraries

chunks.title: Wasabi Legacy Cleanup — Migration Guidance
chunks.content:
If you decide to reclaim space from legacy Wasabi paths:

Do NOT delete legacy paths until you confirm:
1) No scheduled tasks reference them
2) New bucket/tree contains all required history
3) Retention/immutability requirements are satisfied

Recommended approach:
- Start with inventory + compare for a bounded subtree (like Company/er sigs)
- Only then decide delete/move

Verification before cleanup:
- Check all scheduled tasks: Get-ScheduledTask | Select-Object -Expand Actions
- Check all scripts for remote references: Select-String -Path "C:\Backups\*.ps1","C:\Scripts\*.ps1" -Pattern "wasabi-" -SimpleMatch
- For Ubuntu: grep -r "wasabi" /opt/backup/ /usr/local/sbin/

Measure legacy subtree size:
rclone size "wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/files/live/company" --fast-list --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

chunks.title: Status Vocabulary — Active vs Legacy vs Unknown
chunks.content:
Standard status labels used across all backup documentation:

- Active: Confirmed by current scripts, tasks, and schedules. These paths are being written to by running automation.
- Legacy: Exists historically in Wasabi but not referenced by current automation. Data may overlap with active paths. Do not delete without full verification.
- Unknown: Needs verification. Could be active or legacy — check scheduled tasks, scripts, and recent object timestamps to determine.

To verify a path's status:
1) Check if any scheduled task or cron job references it
2) Check if any active script writes to it
3) Check last-modified timestamps of objects in the path
4) If recent timestamps exist but no automation found, investigate further before labeling

chunks.title: Security Rules — Secrets Management
chunks.content:
Critical security rules for backup operations:

- Never store or paste real access keys, secret keys, passwords, or MFA codes in knowledge files, documentation, or chat
- Store secrets only in protected locations: C:\ProgramData\secrets\... (Windows) or equivalent secure paths
- Reference secret file paths only, never the secret values
- Use redaction patterns in examples: AKIA..., ****
- If credentials appear accidentally, treat as compromised and advise rotation without reprinting the values

SMTP secret handling on win-cube:
- SMTP password stored as AES-keyed SecureString
- Both the AES key file and encrypted blob are readable by SYSTEM
- Confirmed that SYSTEM can decrypt the SMTP secret for sending backup notification emails

rclone config: C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf contains Wasabi credentials — protect this file appropriately.

chunks.title: Win-Cube SQL Backup — Tiered Retention Layout
chunks.content:
SQL backups on win-cube use a tiered retention layout:

Path structure: wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/databases/{tier}/{DatabaseName}/{DatabaseName}_Backup_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.bak

Tiers:
- daily/ — daily full backups per database
- weekly/ — weekly full backups per database
- monthly/ — monthly full backups per database

Each tier folder contains one subfolder per database. Known databases include: SuperiorState, UserManager, InstantKB2014, and others.

Local staging directory: C:\Backups\Databases\
Files are staged locally as {Database}_Backup_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.bak before upload via rclone.

Retention is managed by the backup script (cleanup of old backups per tier).

chunks.title: Win-Cube Websites Backup — Retention Details
chunks.content:
Website backups use two retention tiers:

Weekly: wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/websites/weekly/
- Naming: Websites_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.zip
- Retention: keep last 3 weekly backups

Monthly: wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/websites/monthly/
- Naming: Websites_Monthly_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.zip
- Retention: keep 1 per month for last ~4 months + current month

Source: C:\Websites (IIS website content)
Local staging: C:\Backups\Website\Websites_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.zip

The backup script zips the entire C:\Websites directory and uploads to the appropriate tier folder in Wasabi.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Local Backup Artifact Discovery
chunks.content:
Search for local staging folders on Ubuntu (read-only discovery):

sudo find / -maxdepth 4 -type d \( -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*backups*' -o -iname '*staging*' \) 2>/dev/null | head
sudo find / -maxdepth 5 -type f \( -iname '*.sql.gz' -o -iname '*.tar.gz' \) 2>/dev/null | head

These commands identify where backup artifacts are created locally before being uploaded to Wasabi. Check disk space to ensure staging area has sufficient room:
sudo df -h

chunks.title: Ubuntu mysqldump-clean Helper Script
chunks.content:
On the Ubuntu server, a helper script exists at /usr/local/sbin/mysqldump-clean.

Purpose: Avoids conflicts between Acronis agent libraries and the mysql client. The Acronis agent can set LD_LIBRARY_PATH or similar environment variables that inject incompatible GLIBCXX versions, causing mysqldump to fail.

The mysqldump-clean script provides a clean environment for running mysqldump without these library conflicts.

Known issue: If mysqldump is run directly in a shell where Acronis agent environment is active, it may fail with GLIBCXX version errors. Always use the mysqldump-clean wrapper or ensure a clean environment.

Additional known issue: mysqldump may fail with ERROR 1356 (broken views). Fix by dropping or correcting the problematic views using admin credentials.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Paste Freeze Workaround (XON/XOFF)
chunks.content:
Known issue: When pasting large command outputs or text in an Ubuntu terminal session, the terminal may appear to freeze.

Cause: XON/XOFF flow control. Certain character sequences in pasted text (like Ctrl+S) can trigger flow control stop.

Fix: Run this command before pasting:
stty -ixon

This disables XON/XOFF flow control and prevents paste freezes.

chunks.title: Wasabi Bucket Versioning Strategy Explained
chunks.content:
The SSA backup strategy uses two approaches for historical data recovery:

1) Script-managed tiered retention (SQL backups, websites):
   - The backup script manages daily/weekly/monthly folders
   - Old backups are cleaned up by the script based on retention rules
   - Uses non-versioned bucket: wasabi-backup-ssa

2) Wasabi bucket versioning (file share live mirror):
   - Files are synced as a "live mirror" to wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/.../files/live/
   - No script-managed versions/ folder
   - Wasabi's built-in bucket versioning tracks all object changes
   - Historical recovery is done through Wasabi's version management, not through the backup script
   - This was an explicit design decision to simplify the PowerShell scripts

The naming convention wasabi-lock: suggests "object lock" but the primary intent is versioning/immutable-ish workflow. Confirm actual bucket settings (versioning + any retention/lock rules) inside Wasabi console when convenient.

chunks.title: Quick Triage Checklist — Step-by-Step Order
chunks.content:
When investigating backup issues, follow this order:

A. Confirm Task Scheduler success/failure (Win-Cube):
Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for each of the three tasks. Check LastTaskResult (0 = success).

B. Pull the newest run log for the failing job.

C. Confirm rclone remote reachability:
rclone lsd wasabi-u: and rclone lsd wasabi-lock:

D. For SERVER_22 WSB:
wbadmin get status
wbadmin get versions -backuptarget:F:

E. For Ubuntu:
Check /var/log/server_backup.log
Verify cron is active: sudo crontab -l
Test rclone connectivity: rclone lsd wasabi-linux:

F. Check IONOS Backup Unit Manager console for alerts.

Key principle: Always check the simplest things first (task status, log content) before diving into infrastructure (network, permissions, disk space).

chunks.title: Win-Cube File Shares — Source Directories
chunks.content:
The file shares backup on win-cube mirrors from C:\Shares to Wasabi.

Source subfolders:

- C:\Shares\Finance\ → .../files/live/Finance/

Destination: wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/windows/win-cube/files/live/

The sync uses rclone and relies on Wasabi bucket versioning for historical file recovery. Deleted or modified files on the source will be reflected in the destination, but previous versions are retained by Wasabi's versioning feature.

chunks.title: SMTP Email Notifications — Backup Reports
chunks.content:
The win-cube backup scripts send email notifications after each run using SMTP2GO.

Key details:
- SMTP service: SMTP2GO
- SMTP password is stored as an AES-keyed SecureString
- Both the AES key file and encrypted blob are located in paths readable by SYSTEM
- Confirmed: SYSTEM account can decrypt the SMTP secret and send emails

Email reports indicate backup success or failure. Check the email subject line for status indicators.

If SMTP emails stop arriving:
- Verify SYSTEM can still decrypt the secret (test via one-shot scheduled task)
- Check SMTP2GO service status
- Review backup log for SMTP-related errors
- Verify network connectivity to SMTP2GO endpoints

chunks.title: Restoring from Wasabi SQL Backups
chunks.content:
To restore a SQL Server database from Wasabi backup:

1) Identify the correct .bak file:
rclone lsl wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/databases/{tier}/{DBNAME}/ --max-depth 1 --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

2) Download the .bak file to local staging:
rclone copy wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/databases/{tier}/{DBNAME}/{filename}.bak C:\Backups\Restore\ --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

3) Restore using SSMS or sqlcmd:
RESTORE DATABASE [{DBNAME}] FROM DISK = N'C:\Backups\Restore\{filename}.bak' WITH REPLACE;

Note: For SQL Express, backups are uncompressed. Ensure sufficient disk space for both the .bak download and the restored database.

chunks.title: Restoring from Wasabi Website Backups
chunks.content:
To restore IIS website content from Wasabi backup:

1) List available backups:
rclone lsl wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/websites/{weekly|monthly}/ --max-depth 1 --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

2) Download the desired zip file:
rclone copy wasabi-u:wasabi-backup-ssa/windows/win-cube/websites/{tier}/{filename}.zip C:\Backups\Restore\ --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

3) Extract to restore location:
Expand-Archive -Path C:\Backups\Restore\{filename}.zip -DestinationPath C:\Websites_Restore\

4) Review extracted content before replacing production files.

Weekly backups: last 3 available.
Monthly backups: 1 per month for last ~4 months + current.

chunks.title: Restoring Files from Wasabi Versioned Bucket
chunks.content:
File share backups use Wasabi bucket versioning for historical recovery.

To restore a specific file:
1) Check current version exists:
rclone lsl "wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/windows/win-cube/files/live/Company/path/to/file" --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

2) Download current version:
rclone copy "wasabi-lock:ssa-backup-prod/windows/win-cube/files/live/Company/path/to/file" C:\Restore\ --config C:\ProgramData\rclone\rclone.conf

To restore a previous version:
- Use the Wasabi console or S3 API to list object versions
- Wasabi bucket versioning retains previous versions of overwritten/deleted objects
- Refer to Wasabi documentation for version-specific restore operations

Note: rclone's standard commands work with the current version. For historical versions, you'll typically need the Wasabi web console or an S3-compatible tool that supports versioned object retrieval.

chunks.title: Restoring from Ubuntu MySQL Backups
chunks.content:
To restore a MySQL database from Wasabi backup:

1) List available dumps:
rclone lsl wasabi-linux:wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/databases/{tier}/{DB}/ --max-depth 1

2) Download the desired dump:
rclone copy wasabi-linux:wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/databases/{tier}/{DB}/{filename}.sql.gz /tmp/restore/

3) Decompress and restore:
gunzip /tmp/restore/{filename}.sql.gz
mysql -u root -p {DB} < /tmp/restore/{filename}.sql

Available tiers: daily, weekly, monthly
Active databases: beta_ssa, wave_commissions

Note: Use the mysqldump-clean wrapper environment if restoring on the same server where Acronis agent is active, to avoid GLIBCXX library conflicts.

chunks.title: Restoring Ubuntu Webapps and Server Config
chunks.content:
To restore Ubuntu webapps from Wasabi:

1) List available tarballs:
rclone lsl wasabi-linux:wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/webapps/{tier}/ --max-depth 1

2) Download:
rclone copy wasabi-linux:wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/webapps/{tier}/{filename}.tar.gz /tmp/restore/

3) Extract:
tar xzf /tmp/restore/{filename}.tar.gz -C /tmp/restore/

4) Review extracted content before replacing production files.

To restore server config:
1) rclone lsl wasabi-linux:wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/server-config/{tier}/ --max-depth 1
2) rclone copy wasabi-linux:wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/server-config/{tier}/{filename}.tar.gz /tmp/restore/
3) tar xzf /tmp/restore/{filename}.tar.gz -C /tmp/restore/
4) Carefully review and selectively apply config files — do NOT blindly overwrite system configs.

Naming: webapps_YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM.tar.gz, configs_YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM.tar.gz

chunks.title: SERVER_22 WSB Restore — Overview
chunks.content:
SERVER_22 uses Windows Server Backup (WSB) to local disk F: for bare metal recovery.

To list available recovery points:
wbadmin get versions -backuptarget:F:

To start a recovery (example — system state):
wbadmin start systemstaterecovery -version:{VersionIdentifier} -backuptarget:F:

To start a full server recovery:
- Boot from Windows Server installation media
- Choose "Repair your computer" → "System Image Recovery"
- Select the backup from F:

Backup data location on F:: \WindowsImageBackup\...

IMPORTANT: After a catalog reset (wbadmin delete catalog), always specify -backuptarget:F: explicitly. The catalog reset does NOT delete backup data.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Backup Log Location and Rotation
chunks.content:

chunks.title: Wasabi Bucket Names and Their Purposes
chunks.content:
Two Wasabi buckets are in use:

wasabi-backup-ssa:
- Type: Non-versioned (standard)
- Contains: SQL backups (win-cube), website backups (win-cube), Linux database dumps, Linux webapps tarballs, Linux server-config tarballs
- Also contains legacy/dead trees from earlier configurations
- Accessed via: wasabi-u: (Windows), wasabi-linux: (Ubuntu)

ssa-backup-prod:
- Type: Versioned (Wasabi bucket versioning enabled)
- Contains: Live file share mirror from win-cube
- Purpose: Historical file recovery via versioning instead of script-managed version folders
- Accessed via: wasabi-lock: (Windows)

The bucket naming wasabi-lock: for the versioned remote is a convention suggesting immutability/object-lock workflow.
